Vie

VY -- rhymes with 'tie' and 'sky'. · verb

Hear It

What It Means

To vie to compete eagerly with others in order to achieve or obtain something.

Two rival bakeries vie for the title of best pie at the county fair every summer.

Worked Example

Three chefs enter the same cooking competition, each one determined to serve the most impressive dish and walk away with the trophy.

That eager, head-to-head competing for the same prize is exactly what it means to vie. Unlike 'cooperate,' which means working together, to vie means striving against others for the same goal.

How Vie Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

compete

compete: to strive to win or gain something against others

contend

contend: to struggle or compete for something

strive

strive: to make great efforts to achieve something

Antonyms

yield

yield: to give way or surrender to another

concede

concede: to admit defeat or give up a claim

How Strong Is It? — compete → vie → contend

compete vs. vie

compete vs. vie: Compete is broader and more neutral than vie -- compete can describe any contest, even a low-stakes one, while vie suggests a more eager, determined struggle for something specific.

contend vs. vie

contend vs. vie: Contend can feel more intense than vie: vie usually implies competing for a prize or position, while contend often suggests a tougher, more prolonged struggle, sometimes against an obstacle rather than just a rival.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — vi-/envi-

root — vi-/envi-: to challenge, invite (Old French envier, from Latin invitare)

Put it together

Put it together: Vie traces back to Old French envier, 'to challenge' in card games, itself from Latin invitare, 'to invite' or 'to challenge.' To vie for something, at its root, is to issue a challenge for it -- the same root that gives us the word invite.

Use the root in a new word: invite

Use the root in a new word: invite: The mayor decided to invite every local business to submit a proposal for the new park.

Root Check

Word Choice

Vie almost always appears with 'for,' as in 'vie for attention' or 'vie for the championship,' describing an eager competition for something specific and often limited.
